sections.html:
A Cleburne owner short on time tends to sell directly to a cash buyer. One with time to spare often lists with an agent. The direct route avoids showings, loan approval and an appraisal, which leaves clear title as the main hurdle.

  • Cash buyer: fits an inherited house, a rental with tenants, a pile of deferred repairs or a looming foreclosure date.
  • Agent: fits a well-kept house and a flexible schedule.
  • By owner: fits a seller who enjoys contracts and weeding out buyers.

The county appraisal district keeps its office in Cleburne, the Johnson County seat.

Cleburne sits on U.S. Highway 67, thirty miles south of Fort Worth. It became a permanent settlement on March 23, 1867, when the county needed a central seat to replace Buchanan, and it incorporated in May 1871. A rail line through town opened in 1881, and the Santa Fe built its central machine shops here in 1898 and 1899. That railroad past explains why older neighborhoods near the center look different from newer Dallas-Fort Worth suburbs, and why buyers of older houses ask about wiring and plumbing.

sections.h2: Where to get Cleburne property values
sections.html:
Values come from the Central Appraisal District of Johnson County at 109 N. Main St. in Cleburne. The phone is (817) 648-3000, and a drop box in the front door takes paperwork when the office is closed. Confirm any exemption on your account with the office itself.

sections.h2: Taxes owed at the time of sale
sections.html:
Each year's tax lien arrives January 1 and rides with the land, which means an unpaid year passes to the next owner unless someone pays it. Bills appear around October 1 and go delinquent once January 31 is behind you. Suppose you sell in spring and last year's bill is still open. The buyer's title company will spot it and expect it settled out of your proceeds. A call to the Johnson County tax office gets you a payoff figure. Know that number before you talk price, so every offer can be compared fairly.

Disagree with this year's value? You can protest until the later of May 15 or 30 days after the notice. Homestead owners usually get their notices around April 1, so their clock starts early.

sections.h2: Questions about value or a protest
sections.html:
A Taxpayer Liaison Officer, a role the Tax Code requires in counties with populations above 120,000, can help owners reach the district's services. The district's website links to that office.

Notices can be delivered electronically on request, and Tax Code Section 1.085(a-1) obliges a tax official to honor it. A seller who has moved out of the house will find that useful, since paper notices keep going to the old address.

sections.h2: Exemptions for a Cleburne homeowner or buyer
sections.html:
The school homestead exemption is $140,000, plus $60,000 more for an owner who is older or disabled. A disabled veteran's exemption ranges from $5,000 to $12,000 depending on rating, and one rated 100 percent disabled may be fully exempt on a homestead.

Send your application to the appraisal district before May 1. If you never held the exemption, a buyer who moves in after January 1 can often still claim it for the rest of that year. Your own exemption stays with you, so a buyer applies for theirs.

Check with the City of Cleburne's building inspections office on whether your address has an open or unfinished permit. Get the answer in writing for the title company.

If there is an unfinished project, the cleanest fix is to finish and close the permit. If you can't, say so in writing to any buyer and let them decide how to price it. As-is purchases are common, with known problems disclosed.

sections.h2: What a cash buyer will want to see
sections.html:
Before naming a number, a cash buyer sizes up four points: the house's condition, whether someone lives in it, the taxes and liens owed, and who is allowed to sign. If you hand over those facts, the offer comes faster. A one-page list works: the tax bill and payoff, the loan payoff if any, any lease, any open permit, and any probate paperwork. A short note listing repairs you know about completes the page.

Two practical details help. First, the appraisal district office is open weekdays only, so plan calls and visits for those hours or use the drop box. Second, the district has one email address for general questions, another for exemptions and a third for the review board, so write to the one that matches your question.

After you accept, the title company searches records, asks for payoffs and picks a closing date. A notary witnesses your signature on the deed, and the county clerk records it. Tell the appraisal district about any change your exemption needs, and the buyer will file their own.

Work backward from your deadline. In the first days, gather papers and ask the tax office, the appraisal district and building inspections for their records. Next, collect offers and compare them on price, closing costs and date. After you accept one, the title company needs time to search records and request payoffs, and an inherited or tenant-occupied house adds steps on top. If a foreclosure auction is coming, remember that the sale notice must precede it by at least 21 days, which gives you a hard date to beat. Leave a cushion before any deadline you can't move, since missing paperwork is what usually pushes a closing later.

A lender holding a power of sale in the deed of trust can sell a Cleburne house at a Johnson County courthouse auction without going to court. The borrower gets 20 days after the default notice to bring the loan current.

The borrower must receive the sale notice at least 21 days ahead, and it is also posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk. If the lender sues afterward over a shortfall, the suit must come within two years. Selling before the auction may protect your equity, so act early if a notice has arrived.

Each of these has its own Texas rule.

  • Inherited: a will can be probated within four years. A muniment of title moves title when no administration is required. A small estate affidavit works only for estates worth $75,000 or less, not counting homestead and exempt property, and every heir must agree.
  • Tenant: written notice of 3 days, then a justice court filing, then six days after judgment before a writ of possession. County court appeals are due in 5 days.

Disclose each issue to the buyer from the start. The title company will ask for proof you can sell, such as a court order or a recorded affidavit.

faqs.q: Where is the Johnson County appraisal district office?
faqs.a: 109 N. Main St. in Cleburne. It opens on weekdays from 8:00am to 4:30pm and the phone number is (817) 648-3000.

faqs.q: How old is the city of Cleburne?
faqs.a: It became a permanent settlement on March 23, 1867 and incorporated in May 1871. It replaced Buchanan as the Johnson County seat.

faqs.q: What is the school homestead exemption in Texas?
faqs.a: For school taxes it is $140,000 off a homestead, and an owner who is older or disabled gets $60,000 more.

faqs.q: How much notice comes before a Texas foreclosure auction?
faqs.a: The sale notice has to come at least 21 days ahead of the auction, which is held on a first Tuesday. Before that, the borrower has a 20-day window to reinstate.

faqs.q: Does a Cleburne house with repairs still sell?
faqs.a: Yes, since many buyers take houses as-is. Tell them what you know. Ask Building Inspections about any open permit or code issue, because those most often need attention before closing.
